# The channel topology two reference fixtures declare, pinned as data — the
# cross-language instrument for "one output channel per producing tasklet",
# in the shape `test/fixtures/host_class_decl_keys.txt` uses for declaration
# keys.
#
# Provenance: TRANSCRIBED BY HAND from the Rust reference and checked in. It is
# not derived at test time and no runtime computes it — a golden a runtime
# derives is not a golden, it is a second copy of the thing under test. The two
# sources, read at `c6f5dbfa`:
#
#   hybrid_channel      test/apps/rust_runner/src/channel.rs, HybridChannelRelay
#   commit_block_chain  test/apps/rust_runner/src/steps.rs, TierCommitBlockSteps
#
# `commit_block_chain` is this file's name for the second shape because no
# veneer registers a steps fixture yet; it is `tier_commit_block_steps`'s
# topology, which declares nothing about its handoffs — no SDK does, because the
# runtime derives an inter-tasklet channel's journal codec (from the channel
# kind for a host that ships bytes, `flz_core/src/host/register.rs`).
#
# Five readers pin it: `sdk/node/test/decl-keys.test.mjs`,
# `sdk/ruby/test/decl_keys_test.rb`, `sdk/php/tests/DeclKeysTest.php` and
# `sdk/python/tests/test_decl_keys.py` each build both topologies in their own
# spelling and assert their declaration is these lines; the Rust column values
# are what `sdk/rust`'s builder emits for the two fixtures above.
#
# Columns, `|`-separated, `-` for absent:
#   topology | index | name | kind | producer | consumers | sink
#
# `index` is the channel's position in the declaration — id order is the
# contract. Every column is the DERIVED declaration
# `flz_core::host::register::check` answers with, never a builder's own read:
# `producer` and `consumers` are TASKLET indices in declaration order, `kind`
# is the declared kind after the wiring rule (a sink with no consumer is
# `plugin`, everything else keeps the channel's own kind, so a channel carrying
# both a sink and a consumer stays `inter_task`), and `sink` is the plugin
# descriptor name — which the record now carries as a `sink` link, so the core
# derives it rather than being told a channel name and nothing else.

# hybrid_channel — a flow class. One entry, one producer whose single output
# channel carries a plugin sink AND an inter-tasklet consumer.
# Tasklets: 0 hybrid_producer_tasklet, 1 hybrid_consumer_tasklet.
hybrid_channel | 0 | input | entry | - | 0 | -
hybrid_channel | 1 | hybrid_indicator | inter_task | 0 | 1 | hybrid_indicator

# commit_block_chain — a structured steps class with the same hybrid shape
# mid-chain.
# Tasklets: 0 tier_commit_a, 1 block_b.
commit_block_chain | 0 | in | entry | - | 0 | -
commit_block_chain | 1 | mid | inter_task | 0 | 1 | mid

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# refusals — one row per reference refusal. Columns, `|`-separated:
#   refusal | topology | steps | needs
#
# `refusal` is the code of a `TopologyIssue` variant of
# `flz_core/src/host/issue.rs` (`topology.<snake_case>`), or `ok` for a
# well-formed shape whose derived lines follow it in the seven-column table
# above. `test/sdk_conformance/topology_check_test.exs` pairs the two files: a
# variant with no row fails naming the variant, a row naming no variant fails
# naming the row. The only exempt variants are the `unrowed` lines at the end.
#
# `steps` are `;`-separated, in a language-neutral spelling every interpreter
# maps to its own builder:
#   entry(<chan>)              declare an entry channel
#   <x>.into(<task>)           wire x into a tasklet; the result is that
#                              tasklet's output channel, addressed by its role
#   <x>.map.into(<task>)       a transform link before the terminator
#   <x>.filter.into(<task>)    the same link, declared with the SDK's filter
#   <x>.flat_map.into(<task>)  the same link, declared with the SDK's flat_map
#   <x>.key.into(<task>)       a key link before the terminator
#   <x>.map                    a chain nothing closes
#   <x>.sink(<name>)           terminate x on the plugin layer, naming it
#   <x>.sink                   the same, leaving the name derived
#   <x>.call(<target>)         end x in a call to the instance <target>, with a
#                              500 ms deadline, its Response channel
#                              (`<x's channel>.response`) wired into the
#                              tasklet that produces x
#   <x>.call_factory(<factory>)  the same, calling the factory <factory>
#   <x>.call_factory_nocreate(<factory>)  the same, with `create: false`
#   <x>.call_deadline(<ms>)    the same as `call(pricing)`, with deadline <ms>
#   <x>.call_unread(<target>)  `call(<target>)` with its Response channel
#                              wired into nothing
#   <x>.named(<name>)          override x's derived channel name
#   <x>.keyed                  opt x into output identity
#   <x>.retry_max(<n>)         the channel's attempt ceiling
#   <x>.on_full(<policy>)      drop_nothing | drop_newest | drop_oldest
#   merge(<task>, <x>, <x>…)   one merge over the listed sources
#   branch(<x>, <n>)           the branch sugar's arity
#   <task>.mailbox(<n>)        the tasklet's per-Cell mailbox capacity
#   class.run(<tree>)          the class's `run`, as the tree's JSON: "flow",
#                              "steps", {"flow":{"exactly":...}} or
#                              {"steps":{"each":...,"on_failure":...}}; absent
#                              is flow
#   class.durable(<tree>)      the class's `durable`, as the tree's JSON: false,
#                              "local", "remote", {"local":{"sleep_after":ms}};
#                              absent is local
#   shorthand(<id>|-, <sink>|-, <input>|-)
#                              one §5 short form, a flow relay declaration
#                              carrying a tasklet body: the factory id, the
#                              plugin sink and the entry channel name, each `-`
#                              when the row leaves it unwritten. The step
#                              declares NO builder topology — it is the whole
#                              relay. A second step in one row declares a
#                              short form that runs in steps, so a collision
#                              crosses runs
#   shorthand(...).noout       the same, on a body declaring no output
#   shorthand(...).topology    the same, on a declaration that also carries a
#                              topology body
#
# tasklet palette — the interpreter binds each role to one fixture tasklet
# of its own SDK:
#   plain         single mode, wall clock, no cell keys
#   second        a second plain tasklet under its own name
#   twin          a distinct tasklet declaring the SAME name as `plain`
#   static        cell_keys ["a","b"], cells_for NOT overridden
#   routed        cell_keys ["a","b"], cells_for overridden
#   dynamic       dynamic cell mode
#   nochange      logical clock over a tasklet that journals nothing
#   eventtime     event-time clock
#
# `needs` is `-`, or the surface the row needs. An SDK whose manifest or
# documented subset lacks that surface skips the row BY NAME and the seam test
# counts the skip against the declared surface. The surfaces named here:
#   merge      a merge terminator
#   branch     the branch sugar
#   steps      a class that runs in steps
#   detached   a tasklet no entry can reach — unauthorable in a fluent
#              builder, where a node exists only once something wires it
#   untyped_tree  a settings tree written as data, which can put a setting
#              under a parent that does not carry it. Rust and Java cannot
#              write one: their tree is types, so each of these rows is a
#              compile-fail fixture there instead
#   shorthand  the §5 single-tasklet short form. Every SDK carries it, so no
#              manifest may lack this one
#   call       the `call(...)` end. Every SDK carries it, so no manifest may
#              lack this one
#   shorthand_typed_output  a short form on a tasklet whose output the SDK can
#              see at declaration time. Rust, Java and Python (return hint)
#              can; Node, Ruby, PHP and Elixir cannot

# `long_channel_name` declares a 256-character `named(...)`: one byte past the
# metadata region's one-byte length prefix, which is the whole of what the row
# is testing. It is the one row whose steps column carries a literal that long.

topology.duplicate_channel         | dup_channel      | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.named(in); plain.sink                                | -
topology.node_identity_collision   | dup_node         | entry(in); in.into(plain); in.into(twin)                                              | -
topology.channel_name_too_long     | long_channel_name| entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.named(nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnn) | -
topology.branch_too_few_arms       | branch_one_arm   | entry(in); in.into(plain); branch(plain, 1)                                           | branch
topology.cycle                     | cycle            | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.into(second); second.into(plain)                     | -
topology.unreachable_tasklet     | detached_node    | entry(in); in.into(plain); second.into(plain)                                         | detached
topology.cells_for_missing      | keys_no_router   | entry(in); in.into(static)                                                            | -
topology.key_by_on_unkeyable_target | key_on_static    | entry(in); in.key.into(routed)                                                        | -
topology.duplicate_key_by          | dup_key_by       | entry(in); in.key.key.into(plain)                                                     | -
topology.transform_after_terminal  | map_after_sink   | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.sink(out); plain.map.into(second)                    | -
topology.transform_after_key_by    | map_after_key    | entry(in); in.key.map.into(plain)                                                     | -
topology.dangling_transform_chain  | dangling_chain   | entry(in); in.into(plain); in.map                                                     | -
topology.unkeyed_edge_into_dynamic_tasklet | unkeyed_dynamic  | entry(in); entry(other); in.key.into(dynamic); other.into(dynamic)                    | -
topology.mailbox_capacity_zero     | mailbox_zero     | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.mailbox(0)                                           | -
topology.mailbox_capacity_too_large | mailbox_huge     | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.mailbox(2000000)                                     | -
topology.duplicate_plugin_sink     | dup_sink         | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.sink(out); plain.sink(out)                           | -
topology.channel_ends_twice        | call_beside_sink | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.sink(out); plain.call(pricing)                    | call
topology.call_outside_per_input_loop | call_once_steps | class.run("steps"); entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.named(ask); plain.call(pricing)   | steps
topology.call_without_key          | call_nocreate_unkeyed | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.named(ask); plain.call_factory_nocreate(agent) | call
topology.call_deadline_zero        | call_deadline_zero | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.named(ask); plain.call_deadline(0)             | call
topology.call_response_unread      | call_unread      | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.named(ask); plain.call_unread(pricing)             | call
topology.keyed_channel_without_plugin_wire | keyed_no_wire    | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.keyed; plain.into(second)                            | -
topology.channel_named_twice       | named_twice      | entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.named(a); plain.sink(b)                              | -
topology.duplicate_sink_name       | two_channels_one_sink | entry(in); in.into(plain); in.into(second); plain.sink(out); second.sink(out)    | -
topology.unservable_clock          | logical_nochange | entry(in); in.into(nochange)                                                          | -
topology.unkeyed_channel_under_effectively_once | eo_unkeyed_sink  | class.run({"flow":{"exactly":"effectively_once"}}); entry(in); in.into(plain); plain.sink(out)  | -
topology.retry_max_zero            | retry_zero       | entry(in); in.retry_max(0); in.into(plain)                                            | -
topology.dropping_policy_under_effectively_once | eo_sheds         | class.run({"flow":{"exactly":"effectively_once"}}); entry(in); in.on_full(drop_newest); in.into(plain) | -
topology.correction_without_event_time | correction_wall  | class.run({"flow":{"exactly":{"effectively_once":{"correction_ms":60000}}}}); entry(in); in.into(plain) | -
topology.correction_window_zero    | correction_zero  | class.run({"flow":{"exactly":{"effectively_once":{"correction_ms":0}}}}); entry(in); in.into(eventtime) | -

topology.merge_too_few_sources     | merge_one_source | entry(in); merge(plain, in)                                                           | merge
topology.duplicate_merge_source    | merge_same_twice | entry(in); entry(other); merge(plain, in, in)                                         | merge
topology.edge_already_wired        | edge_rewired     | entry(in); in.map.into(plain); in.into(plain)                                         | -
topology.at_checkpoint_without_max_delay | hold_no_delay    | class.run({"flow":{"exactly":{"effectively_once":{"ack":{"checkpoint":{"outputs":"at_checkpoint"}}}}}}); entry(in); in.into(plain) | -
topology.effectively_once_without_persistence | eo_in_memory | class.run({"flow":{"exactly":"effectively_once"}}); class.durable(false); entry(in); in.into(plain) | -

# The settings tree's misplaced settings: each is written under a parent that
# does not carry it, and the answer names the setting and that parent.

topology.unknown_field             | correction_under_steps | class.run({"steps":{"correction_ms":5000}}); entry(in); in.into(plain)        | untyped_tree
topology.unknown_field             | exactly_under_steps | class.run({"steps":{"exactly":"effectively_once"}}); entry(in); in.into(plain)  | untyped_tree
topology.unknown_field             | sleep_after_in_memory | class.durable({"false":{"sleep_after":1000}}); entry(in); in.into(plain)       | untyped_tree
topology.invalid_setting           | kind_literal     | class.run("bounded"); entry(in); in.into(plain)                                       | untyped_tree

# The §5 short-form refusals. Their codes are the authoring contract's, not
# `flz_core`'s: the core never sees a short form, so these rows are exempt from
# the issue-variant pairing and checked against §5's list instead.
topology.short_form_with_topology  | shorthand_with_topology       | shorthand(plain, out, -).topology                                         | shorthand

topology.duplicate_factory_id      | shorthand_duplicate_id        | shorthand(plain, out, -); shorthand(plain, twin_sink, -)                  | shorthand
